=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/unblock_actions.py:639-646 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_closing_keyword_re` accepts any qualified `owner/repo#<item>` closing reference without checking that the prefix is the issue's own repository, so a same-repo-head PR that only says "Refs #N" here but "Closes other/repo#N" is chosen as the implementation PR.
  WHY: reset_ops then posts the judge's note on that unrelated PR, dispatches its review and removes the issue's stop label while the real problem stays unfixed. Severity disagreement: minimax and luna rated this MAJOR, glm rated it NIT; glm says implement.yml:403 is equally permissive, so the result is misdirected work rather than divergence.
- scripts/unblock_actions.py:674-707 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: `same_repo` in `implementation_pr_candidate` checks only `headRepository.nameWithOwner`, never the PR's base repository, and the GraphQL `source{... on PullRequest{...}}` selection at scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1882 does not request `repository{nameWithOwner}`. As a result, a PR opened in another repository from a branch of this repository is accepted.
  WHY: The foreign PR number is returned as `implementation_pr`. unblock_run_ops then comments on `repos/${REPOSITORY}/issues/<n>` (unblock_judge.sh:1250) and dispatches review with `-R "${REPOSITORY}"` (unblock_judge.sh:1453), so it acts on an unrelated local issue or PR and silently drops the real block. The suggested fix is about 3 lines.
- scripts/unblock_actions.py:636-645 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: `_closing_keyword_re` requires whitespace after the keyword, so it rejects the colon form "Closes: #N".
  WHY: Such a PR is not identified, and reset falls back to `/approved`. Luna cites scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:34 and tests/test_lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:144-154 as treating colon forms as closing syntax. Severity disagreement: gemini MAJOR, luna NIT. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash dispute the finding: implement.yml:403/6378 also require `[[:space:]]+`, so a colon-form PR never triggers the `existing_pr` refusal.
- scripts/unblock_actions.py:639-646 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The ASCII-only class `[^A-Za-z0-9_-]` in `_closing_keyword_re` differs from implement.yml's POSIX `[^[:alnum:]_-]` (implement.yml:403, 6378; orchestrate_poll_process.sh:23702) when non-ASCII letters sit next to the keyword.
  WHY: implement.yml would accept the PR as `existing_pr` while the new code returns `reason="none"` and falls back to `/approved`, so the issue loops back to needs-human.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1865-1911 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `unblock_resolve_implementation_pr` calls `gh api graphql` directly, without `gh_retry`, and on failure logs `outcome=unavailable reason=read_failed` and returns 0. The Python parse call at line 1888 is also unguarded.
  WHY: Routing is on by default, so a single transient GraphQL failure reverts to `/approved`, and the issue re-enters the #9733 `existing_pr` loop. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 considers this fail-open behaviour correct (it matches `unblock_resolve_ci_owner`); z-ai_glm-5_3-flash lists it only as hardening.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1449-1454 (reached from scripts/unblock_actions.py:715-736 `_existing_pr_route_ops`) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `dispatch_review` op that the new routing emits runs `gh workflow run` with no `_has_active_autofix_run` guard and no cycle-local dedup tracker. Minimax adds that it also has no `gh_retry` and no fallback to `review_autofix.yml`, unlike `_dispatch_review_for_conflicts` (orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28644).
  WHY: The unblock judge and orchestrator stall recovery can both dispatch review on the same PR. The concurrency group then cancels the pending run and raises spurious cancelled/timed-out alerts (orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28667-28674). Severity disagreement: gemini and minimax MAJOR, luna and glm NIT. glm notes the executor behaviour predates this PR, and anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 says the PR reuses the existing op without weakening any guard.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20573 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_existing_pr_routing_enabled` uses `${UNBLOCK_EXISTING_PR_ROUTING_ENABLED-true}` (single dash) rather than `${...:-true}`. Minimax notes the same form at scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1849 and the `:-` form at line 3216.
  WHY: Gemini says a set-but-empty value disables the feature. Minimax says today's `""` case arm keeps it on, but the inconsistency is a hazard for future callers. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 disputes the finding: line 3216 sets the default first, and the `""|true` arm treats empty as on.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1847-1855 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `unblock_existing_pr_routing_enabled` logs an invalid flag value only as an informational UNBLOCK_JUDGE line, with no `::warning::`, and does not trim whitespace, unlike the Python helper's `.strip()` at scripts/unblock_actions.py:631.
  WHY: A typo such as `ture` silently disables routing on the unblock path, while the orchestrator helper (orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20578) warns. A value like `true ` is "off" in shell but "on" in Python.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20594-20623 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When `_stall_route_open_impl_pr` gets rc=2 or rc=3 from the dispatch, the caller arms (20738-20748, 20811-20821) `return 1` without a backoff or retry counter.
  WHY: A persistent dispatch failure retries on every poll tick (288 STALL_SKIP lines per 24h) with no sign of a real failure. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 says the return of 1 matches the existing "no action, do not increment" contract (orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28146, 28174, 28182).
- scripts/unblock_actions.py:1271-1274 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `override_guard` branch still appends `_approve` (adds `ai:awaiting-approval` and posts `/approved`) even when `context.json` carries `implementation_pr`. Routing is wired only into `reset_ops` (988-996), yet README.md:127 says the scope-blocked/destructive-blocked reset routes.
  WHY: A scope-blocked issue with an open `ai/issue-<n>` PR that is judged `override_guard` hits the same `existing_pr` no-op loop as #9733. agents.d documents this as an intended residual.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Apply the same rule to the orchestrator's stall-recovery auto-approve: when the issue already has an open implementation PR, do not post /approved; dispatch review on the PR." README.md:127 and changelog.d/9809-unblock-existing-pr-routing.md claim "stall recovery's `auto_approve` / `retrigger_implement` dispatch the PR's review" without qualification.
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh standalone stall-recovery `auto_approve` arm (line 27054, posts /approved at 27067-27072) and `retrigger_implement` arm (line 27081, posts /approved at 27100-27105); alternatively qualify README.md / changelog.d / agents.d fragment as "orchestrator-managed" only
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: `_stall_route_open_impl_pr` is called only from the managed arms of `execute_stall_recovery_action` (orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20740/20813, 20738-20748/20811-20821), standalone arms at 27054/27081 (case block at 26952) have no diff hunk and post `/approved` via `gh_retry gh api .../comments` unconditionally, tests/test_stall_existing_impl_pr_routing.py covers only managed arms, the managed path meets the issue's literal wording but README/changelog overstate coverage (severity disagreement: sonnet/glm NIT, gemini/minimax/luna MAJOR)
- requirement: README row says the reset for `needs-human`, `blocked`, `scope-blocked`, `destructive-blocked` and `implement-diagnose-failed` routes to the PR; issue covers "needs-human, blocked, a guard stop or implement-diagnose-failed"
  expected_change_site: scripts/unblock_actions.py `plan()` override_guard branch (lines 1271-1274); apply `_existing_pr_route_ops` before `_approve`
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The override_guard branch calls `ops += _approve(...)` directly. `test_issue_reset_routes_to_open_implementation_pr` covers only `reset_ops`, not `actions.plan(...)` with verdict=override_guard. The agents.d fragment documents the gap; the README does not. (anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 judges this out of scope, not a gap.)
- requirement: "Add tests in tests/ for the routed path, the flag-off path and the no-PR path."
  expected_change_site: tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py (standalone auto_approve / retrigger_implement arms with an open implementation PR, asserting /approved is NOT posted)
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: No new test covers the standalone arms. The existing `test_standalone_*` tests assert reaching /approved, and tests/test_stall_existing_impl_pr_routing.py extracts only two helpers via `_helpers()` and never invokes the standalone arm body.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/unblock_actions.py:674-677, 698-707; scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1882 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The closes fallback in `implementation_pr_candidate` checks only the head repository of a cross-referencing PR, and the GraphQL query never fetches the base `repository{nameWithOwner}`. A PR from another repository whose head is in this repository and whose author is the pipeline login or OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR passes, and its foreign number becomes `implementation_pr`.
  WHY: reset_ops emits comment and dispatch_review against the local repository (unblock_judge.sh:1250, 1453), so it acts on an unrelated local issue or PR and removes the stop label, which silently drops the real block. implement.yml:427-450 has no such gap.
